problem: Find the slope of the tangent at the point $(\frac{\pi }{3},\,2)$ for the curve $y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)=1.$

feedback.worked_solution:
To find the slope at a point, we use implicit differentiation to calculate the derivative of the curve, assuming that $y=y(x).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{y}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{1/2}+{y}^{1/2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6) \\ \frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2}+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{-1/2}(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}) & =0 \\ \frac{1}{2}{y}^{-1/2}(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}) & =-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2} \\ \frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}) & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{\sqrt{y}}{\sqrt{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

The slope of the tangent at the point $(16,\,4)$ is then given by

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(16,\,4)} \\  & ={(-\frac{\sqrt{y}}{\sqrt{x}})|}_{(16,\,4)} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{4}}{\sqrt{16}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{4} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
